name: Favicon Generator
title: Favicon Generator: ICO, PNG & Apple Icons in One Zip
description: Free favicon generator: favicon.ico, 16–512px PNGs and an Apple touch icon from an image, text or emoji — plus the HTML to paste. No signup.
answer: A favicon generator turns a letter, emoji or image into the icon files a website needs. Create yours below and download one zip with favicon.ico (16, 32 and 48 px), a 180 px Apple touch icon, 192 and 512 px app icons, a web manifest and the HTML to paste.
trust: Every file is drawn and packaged in your browser. Uploaded images never leave your device.
body:
## Free Favicon Generator From Text, Emoji or Image

Three ways to start: type one or two letters, paste an emoji, or upload a logo. Pick a background, shape and padding, and the previews update at real sizes — 16, 32, 48 and 180 pixels — so you can see whether it still reads at the size of a browser tab.

Simple shapes survive best. A detailed logo that works at 512 pixels often turns into a smudge at 16.

## Favicon Generator Online: The Sizes Google Needs

Google needs very little: a square icon of at least 8×8 pixels, ideally larger than 48×48, declared on your homepage ([Google's guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/favicon-in-search)). The other files serve browsers and devices:

| File | Size | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| favicon.ico | 16, 32, 48 px | Browser tabs, Google Search |
| apple-touch-icon.png | 180 px | iPhone and iPad home screens |
| icon-192.png, icon-512.png | 192, 512 px | Android and installable web apps |
| site.webmanifest | — | Lists the app icons ([web.dev](https://web.dev/articles/add-manifest)) |

## Why does my favicon look blurry or invisible?

Usually because a wide logo was squeezed into a square, or thin details vanished at 16 pixels. Use a bold mark or a single letter, leave a little padding, and check contrast against both light and dark browser tabs — a dark icon on a transparent background can disappear in dark mode.

## How do I install the favicons?

Unzip the files into your site root and paste the snippet into the head of every page:

```
<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" sizes="48x48">
<link rel="icon" href="/icon-192.png" type="image/png" sizes="192x192">
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">
<link rel="manifest" href="/site.webmanifest">
```

Make sure robots.txt doesn't block the files: Google fetches favicons with Googlebot-Image.

## Do big sites bother with all these files?

Most do. In our October 2026 analysis of 315 big-brand homepages ([dataset](/resources/technical-seo-baseline-2026-10.json)), 90.8% declared an icon, 66.7% set an Apple touch icon and 21.3% offered an SVG favicon.

After uploading, run the [favicon checker](/tools/favicon-checker) to confirm Google can load a qualifying icon, then check how your site looks when shared with the [link preview tool](/tools/link-preview).

faqs.q: What size should a favicon be?
faqs.a: Provide favicon.ico with 16, 32 and 48 pixel versions, a 180 pixel Apple touch icon and 192 and 512 pixel PNGs. Google requires at least 8×8 and recommends larger than 48×48.

faqs.q: Can I use an emoji as a favicon?
faqs.a: Yes. Type an emoji in the text field and the generator draws it into every file. Emoji rendering follows your device's emoji font, so check the preview before downloading.

faqs.q: Should I use an SVG favicon?
faqs.a: An SVG icon scales perfectly and Google accepts it, but keep favicon.ico as well for older browsers and tools that only look for /favicon.ico.
